([[Duncanville, Texas]]) | college = * [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]] (2016–2018) * [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * [[Conference USA]] All-Freshman Team (2017) * [[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] Newcomer of the Year (2020) * First-team All-Mountain West (2020) | medal_templates = }} '''Jalen Harris''' (born August 14, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]] and the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]]. ==Early life and high school career== Harris was born in [[Dallas|Dallas, Texas]], the son of Karlin Kennedy and Erion Harris, both of whom played basketball at [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]], and has two younger brothers and a sister. His mother gave birth to him at the age of 19 but returned to the floor at SMU for her junior season and graduated as the Mustangs' all-time leader in points, rebounds, blocks, and field-goal percentage. Harris grew up in [[Duncanville, Texas|Duncanville]] and played basketball, football, and baseball. He gave up football after an injury in middle school, after which he trained with his father to become a high-level basketball player. His father formed the travel team Dallas Heroes around his son in middle school.{{cite news |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Born for this: Jalen Harris' path to stardom started early but wasn't easy |url=http://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/born-for-this-jalen-harris-path-to-stardom-started-early-but-wasnt-easy |accessdate=February 23, 2020 |work=Nevada Sports Net |date=February 7, 2020}} He attended [[Duncanville High School]] and grew to 6'3 as a sophomore. As a junior, he averaged 15 points, 4 rebounds, and 2 assists per game and was named the District 8-6A Offensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2015/11/15/boys-basketball-preview-6a-state-champion-plano-west-returns-no-full-time-starters-but-still-boasts-experience/|title=Boys basketball preview: 6A state champion Plano West returns no full-time starters but still boasts experience|last=Jennings|first=Randy|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=November 14, 2015|accessdate=February 23, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2015/03/28/class-6a-dallas-area-all-district-boys-basketball-teams/|title=Class 6A Dallas-area all-district boys basketball teams|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=March 27, 2015|accessdate=February 23, 2020}} He suffered a broken vertebrae during an AAU event, forcing him to miss half of his senior season. Nevertheless, Harris was again named District 8-6A Offensive Player of the Year as a senior.{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2016/03/26/dallas-area-boys-all-district-teams-find-your-star-player-here/|title=Dallas-area boys all-district teams: Find your star player here|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=March 25, 2016|accessdate=February 23, 2020}} He averaged 23 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals per game as a senior and shot 55 percent from the field and 45 percent on three-point attempts. In a game against [[Cedar Hill High School]], Harris scored a career-high 44 points. He was rated as the 16th best player and the ninth-best guard in Texas in his class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. Harris spurned offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] to sign with Louisiana Tech. ==College career== Harris began his collegiate career at [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]]. As a true freshman, he averaged 10.9 points and 3.1 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Conference USA]] All-Freshman team.{{cite web|url=https://www.kolotv.com/content/sports/La-Tech-transfer-Harris-signs-with-Nevada-472418023.html|title=La Tech transfer Harris signs with Nevada|website=KOLOTV.com|date=February 2, 2018|accessdate=February 23, 2020}} As a sophomore, Harris led the Bulldogs in scoring with 15.3 points per game while also averaging 4.4 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.1 steals per game, shooting 44.4 percent from behind the arc. He decided to transfer after 11 games. In January 2018, he signed with [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]] over offers from [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]] and [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks men's basketball|Stephen F. Austin]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2018/01/24/wolf-pack-lands-jalen-harris-high-scoring-guard-louisiana-tech/1064080001/|title=Wolf Pack lands high-scoring guard from LaTech|last=Murray|first=Chris|work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]]|date=January 24, 2018|accessdate=February 22, 2020}} Harris chose the Wolf Pack after attending a game against [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]] after being impressed by coach [[Eric Musselman]] and welcoming fans and sat out the 2018–19 season as a redshirt, during which Nevada finished 29–5. After his redshirt season, coach Musselman left for [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], and Harris entered the transfer portal again the day before the school hired [[Steve Alford]]. Despite receiving interest from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and SMU, Harris decided to stay at Nevada. He missed his second game with his new team with a foot injury and struggled in a game against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], finishing 3-of-19 with nine points. During an eight-game stretch in January 2020, Harris averaged 27 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game. On February 11, he was named Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week by the [[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]] after scoring a career-high 38 points against [[Air Force Falcons men's basketball|Air Force]] and 32 points against [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Diego State]].{{cite news |last1=Ritenhouse |first1=Duke |title=Best in the land: Wolf Pack's Jalen Harris named national player of the week |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/2020/02/11/nevada-basketball-wolf-pack-jalen-harris-ncaa-national-player-week/4725906002/ |accessdate=February 23, 2020 |work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]] |date=February 11, 2020}} He had 29 points, a career-high 14 rebounds, five assists, and two steals in a 82–79 overtime win against [[UNLV Running Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]] on February 12, becoming the 11th Nevada player to tally at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game.{{cite news |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=The game that turned Nevada's Jalen Harris into a scoring monster |url=http://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/the-game-that-turned-nevadas-jalen-harris-into-a-scoring-monster |accessdate=February 23, 2020 |work=Nevada Sports Net |date=February 14, 2020}} Harris is the first Nevada player since [[Nick Fazekas]] in 2006 to have four or more 30-point games in a season.{{cite news |last1=Ritenhouse |first1=Duke |title=Nevada basketball: Wolf Pack's Jalen Harris is on a scoring tear |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/2020/02/03/nevada-basketball-wolf-pack-jalen-harris-leads-mountain-west-scoring/4648461002/ |accessdate=February 23, 2020 |work=[[Reno Gazette-Journal]] |date=February 3, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Harris was named to the First Team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] and conference newcomer of the year.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2020/3/3/mountain-west-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx |title=Mountain West Announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 3, 2020 |accessdate=March 3, 2020}} He averaged 21.7 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Nevada looks for home win vs No. 5 San Diego St. |url=https://lancasteronline.com/sports/basketball/college/nevada-looks-for-home-win-vs-no-san-diego-st/article_a11604be-a963-5f5d-ab37-b58d605a874f.html |accessdate=March 24, 2020 |work=Lancaster Online |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 28, 2020}} Following the season, Harris declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Nevada's Jalen Harris makes initial cut for NBA draft combine invitation |url=http://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/nevadas-jalen-harris-makes-initial-cut-for-nba-draft-combine-invitation |accessdate=September 17, 2020
